metadata.title: The Relationship between the School Resources index; Gender; Age and Mathematics Achievement in TIMSS 2019 survey: Multilevel analysis

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses TIMSS 2019 Moroccan fourth-grade student data accessed via the IEA International Database (IDB) Analyzer. It reports a multilevel (two-level) modeling strategy with students nested in schools (257 schools; 7500 students), but it does not state the use of TIMSS sampling weights or any replicate-weight scheme. Because the analysis is implemented in R (lme4/lmerTest) and SPSS 20, the manuscript does not document whether complex survey design weights were applied; therefore, readers should treat the estimates as potentially not fully adjusted for TIMSS’s complex sampling. For replication, analysts should use the appropriate TIMSS student/sampling weights (and replicate weights if available) when estimating multilevel models with PV-based achievement scores.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used TIMSS 2019 database for Morocco only, restricted to fourth-grade students and to the mathematics achievement outcome. The dependent variable is the average mathematics achievement score derived from the five plausible values. The study imputes missing data using the R mice package before fitting the multilevel models; no additional exclusions (e.g., item nonresponse thresholds) are described in the provided text.

main_findings.performance_metrics: Multilevel random-intercept/slope models (M0–M4). School-level variance explained: 39.41% (ICC=0.3941). Age effect (M1): γ10=-4.84 (SD=1.19), p<.05. Gender effect (M2): γ20=-4.42 (SD=1.68), p<.05 (girls reference). RMI effect (M3): γ30=8.23 (SD=2.43), p<.05. GSR effect (M4): γ40=14.37 (SD=8.2), p=.08.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TIMSS 2019 Morocco Grade 4 Mathematics (PVs) the study leveraged Age, Gender, Resources for Mathematics Instruction (RMI), and General School Resources (GSR) to model mathematics achievement, finding that achievement decreases with age, girls score higher than boys, and both RMI and GSR are positively associated with achievement (with GSR only marginally significant). This indicates that strengthening mathematics-specific instructional resources (and, to a lesser extent, broader school resources) may support higher mathematics performance among Moroccan grade 4 students, while accounting for student demographics and school-level clustering.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes TIMSS 2019 Moroccan fourth-grade students (7500 students across 257 schools) and models mathematics achievement using multilevel random-intercept/slope models. The dependent variable is the average mathematics achievement score derived from the five plausible values, and missing data are imputed using the R mice package. The empty model shows substantial between-school variation (ICC=0.3941; school-level variance explained 39.41%), justifying hierarchical modeling. In the full models, age is negatively associated with mathematics achievement (γ10=-4.84, p<.05), and girls outperform boys (γ20=-4.42, p<.05, girls as reference). Mathematics-specific resources (RMI) show a positive association (γ30=8.23, p<.05), while general school resources (GSR) are positive but only marginally significant (γ40=14.37, p=.08). The manuscript does not report the use of TIMSS sampling/replicate weights, so results may not be fully representative under complex survey design.
